sentences.text: Heard Sri S.Nava Kishore, the learned counsel for petitioner and the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent-State.

3. Perused the record.
4.
In Crime No.146 of 2024 there are nine accused.
The present anticipatory bail petition is filed by A.9.
The allegations are that the victim-cum-de facto complainant has been doing paddy business.
He had paid various amounts of money to A.1 to A.8 on their promise that they would supply paddy.
Despite demands, they failed to supply the paddy and they spent away the money received from the victim-cum-de facto complainant.
Notice was issued to them but there was no response.
5. The specific allegation against A.9, who is the present petitioner, is that he was a mediator between the victim-cum-de facto complainant and A.1 to A.8.
It is stated that A.9 introduced the rest of the accused.
6. From the facts narrated above, it is clear that the petitioner/ A.9
did not receive any money from the de facto complainant and he did not prevent A.1 to A.8 from supplying paddy and did not advise them not to return the money to the de facto complainant.
According to the learned counsel for petitioner, the petitioner/A.9 has been working in Agro Asia Company and by his occupation he gives suggestions to the farmers to secure higher yield of crops.
That a civil case is given a criminal colour and the police are after him without any crime being committed by him.

7. As one would notice from the complaint lodged by the de facto complainant before the learned Magistrate, which was thereafter referred under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. to police, the victim was expressing his grievance before the police by lodging written information and they did not take it up and he moved his grievance before the police superiors who also did not respond and in those circumstances he had filed the private complaint which was finally, at the orders of the learned Magistrate, was registered as F.I.R.
It is seen from the record and the submissions of the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor disclosed that no effective investigation has taken place so far.
From the record available, there are no constituting facts to attract any of the penal provisions mentioned in the F.I.R.
In such circumstances, custodial interrogation does not seem necessary.
Hence, prayer is granted.
8. In the result, this Criminal Petition is allowed.

In the event of arrest of the petitioner herein/A.9,
he shall be enlarged on bail on his executing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand only) with two sureties for a like sum each to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer.
The petitioner/A.9 shall mark his attendance before the Investigating Officer on 1st and 15th of every month between 10.00 AM and 1.00 PM till filing of the charge sheet.

The petitioner/A.9 shall make himself available for investigation by a police officer as and when required, and he shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any persons acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
He shall not indulge in similar acts of crime.
